summary: Maps NETCONF onto the Blocks Extensible Exchange Protocol (BEEP), a framework for building application protocols. It specifies how NETCONF sessions and messages are carried over a BEEP channel. This RFC is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4744 describes how NETCONF messages travel over BEEP, including session setup, message exchange, and security. The RFC is Historic and was updated by RFC 8996.

questions: what port does netconf over beep use
is netconf over beep still used
subtitle: The former BEEP transport mapping for NETCONF device-management sessions.

tldr.problem: NETCONF is designed to run over different application protocols, so each transport needs a defined mapping. This RFC specifies the mapping onto BEEP.
tldr.mechanism: A manager and agent establish a BEEP connection, negotiate security, open the NETCONF profile channel, exchange hello messages, and carry RPC requests and replies on that channel.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4744 is Historic and was updated by RFC 8996. Its BEEP transport mapping is not a current specification.

today: RFC 4744 is Historic and was updated by RFC 8996.

sections.title: Why Use BEEP for NETCONF
sections.content:
NETCONF is a protocol for managing network devices and is designed to use different application protocols. RFC 4744 defines its mapping onto the Blocks Extensible Exchange Protocol (BEEP), which carries XML and supports exchanges initiated by either peer.

Either the manager or the agent can initiate the BEEP connection. This can help when devices connect intermittently or when a device needs to initiate a management connection through a firewall or network address translator.
sections.plainLanguage: BEEP can carry XML, and either side can start the connection. This lets a managed device call the manager when it cannot accept an incoming connection.

sections.title: Establishing a Secure Session
sections.content:
The initiator connects to the listener on TCP port 831. During BEEP greetings, both sides announce TLS support and may announce SASL support. If both support TLS and it is to be used, the listener starts a TLS channel, after which both peers send new greetings.

The agent advertises the NETCONF profile; the manager must not advertise it. If the manager authenticates with SASL, the initiator opens a separate channel for that exchange and closes it when authentication ends. SASL PLAIN must not be used over an unencrypted channel.
sections.plainLanguage: The peers first establish the BEEP connection and negotiate a secure channel. The agent identifies itself as the NETCONF endpoint, and any SASL exchange uses a separate channel.

sections.title: Exchanging NETCONF Messages
sections.content:
The manager opens a BEEP channel using the profile URI http://iana.org/beep/netconf. NETCONF messages use content type text/xml. The manager and agent exchange <hello> messages on the channel to learn each other's capabilities.

The manager sends an <rpc> request in a BEEP MSG message. The agent returns an <rpc-reply> in a BEEP RPY message on the same channel; either message may span multiple BEEP frames. Closing channel 0 ends the session and releases locks.
sections.plainLanguage: The manager opens a channel for NETCONF, and both sides exchange capability lists. Commands and replies then use the same channel until it closes.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content:
Configuration data may include passwords, user names, service descriptions, and topology information. The mapping uses TLS for confidentiality and server authentication; the client must validate the server certificate and should reject an invalid certificate by default. If TLS did not authenticate the client, the server should offer SASL profiles.

Implementations must support DIGEST-MD5 when TLS is not established. The RFC assigns TCP port 831 to NETCONF over BEEP. The batch metadata marks RFC 4744 Historic and records that RFC 8996 updated it.
sections.plainLanguage: Device settings may contain sensitive data, so the connection needs encryption and authentication. RFC 4744 is now Historic; RFC 8996 updates it.
